findings.title: Jinja built-ins read as missing context fields
findings.problem: extract_placeholder_names treats any plain {{ name }} as a context requirement. loop / loop.index inside a for block and literals true, false, none, True, False, None match _PLAIN_REFERENCE and are not excluded; loop_locals holds only for/set targets.
findings.impact: Derived requirement no producer can satisfy yields a false ERROR labelled renders empty, contradicting the AR-18 no-false-ERROR claim; blocks the save under strict. Reachability: live for any agent task using loop.index.
findings.recommendation: In extract_placeholder_names skip roots loop, true, false, none, True, False, None (and add loop to the for-block locals) before recording a placeholder name.
findings.check_notes: derive.py skips loop/true/false/none roots via _JINJA_BUILTIN_NAMES; tests added

findings.title: New contracts modules lack future annotations import
findings.problem: code-quality.md asks new modules to add from __future__ import annotations; none of the 11 new modules under src/codemie/workflows/contracts/ nor validation/tool_schemas.py has it.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard for new modules is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Add from __future__ import annotations after the module docstring in each new module (contracts/*.py and validation/tool_schemas.py).
findings.check_notes: from __future__ import annotations present in every contracts module and tool_schemas.py

fix.change: from __future__ import annotations added to every new contracts module and tool_schemas.py

findings.title: Size cap measured on lossy encode
findings.problem: security-patterns.md forbids lossy repair (errors=replace) before a decision on untrusted input; the contract size cap uses text.encode(utf-8, errors=replace), so a lone surrogate is counted as one byte instead of being rejected. The same pattern is at contracts/reader.py:103.
findings.impact: The size-limit decision is made on data that differs from what was sent.
findings.recommendation: Encode strictly and treat UnicodeEncodeError as a rejection; apply the same in contracts/reader.py:103.
findings.check_notes: utf8_size encodes strictly; input_contract and reader reject not_encodable; tests added

fix.change: strict utf8_size helper; unencodable text rejected as not_encodable in input_contract and reader

findings.title: Analysis failure ignores state-level strict
findings.problem: Spec failure isolation requires an unexpected whole-analysis failure to reject under workflow or state strict, but failure_report sets reported_as from settings.mode only, so a state-level validation: strict does not make it reject.
findings.impact: Partial on a required spec requirement: a crashed analysis silently saves a workflow that declared strict on a state.
findings.recommendation: In failure_report set reported_as BLOCKS when the workflow mode or any state's effective mode is strict, not only settings.mode.
findings.check_notes: failure_report blocks when workflow or any state mode is strict; tests added

fix.change: failure_report blocks when the workflow or any state mode is strict

findings.title: Render failure turns a rejecting record into INFO
findings.problem: _finish degrades an unrenderable record to _fallback_class(mode), which is INFO in warn mode; the fallback ignores the record's kind and outcome, so a declared ERROR that would block (_REJECTING_KINDS) becomes informational if its message fails to render.
findings.impact: A rendering bug fails open exactly where a rejection was due and the save goes through. Reachability of a render failure was not established.
findings.recommendation: Compute reported_as outside the try block, or make the fallback honour the record's kind and outcome so a rejecting ERROR still reports BLOCKS when its message cannot render.
findings.check_notes: _finish computes reported_as before rendering; fallback record keeps it; test added

fix.change: _finish decides reported_as before rendering, so the fallback record keeps its class

findings.title: Lookup budget spent by tools that need no service call
findings.problem: Spec bounds the 25-lookup budget to built-in find_tool_by_name lookups, but _mandatory_parameters counts every distinct tool key via len(self._lookups), including static MCP (in memory) and plugin tools.
findings.impact: A workflow with many MCP or plugin tools degrades later built-in tools to UNVERIFIED lookup_budget_exhausted without any service call spent; strict then blocks the save.
findings.recommendation: Count against LOOKUP_BUDGET only built-in find_tool_by_name lookups; keep static MCP and plugin tools out of the budget and the _lookups count.
findings.check_notes: budget counts only built-in service lookups (_needs_service_call, _service_lookups); test added

fix.change: lookup budget and result.lookups count only built-in service lookups; MCP and plugin tools are free

findings.title: Filtered field is ERROR even with unknown sources
findings.problem: AC-9 says a required field excluded by include_in_iterator_context is ERROR when all sources are known, else UNVERIFIED. _branch_context marks it REMOVED and _outcome returns ERROR before consulting unknown_contribution (always true via the undeclared initial input). test_ac4_reset_key_stays_error_with_an_unknown_initial_input asserts the same for AC-5.
findings.impact: Partial on a required criterion. The runtime does drop the key, so ERROR is defensible, but a declared requirement then rejects the save where the ticket requires UNVERIFIED.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether a required field excluded by include_in_iterator_context is UNVERIFIED when any source on the path is unknown (ticket AC-9) or stays a definite ERROR (current behaviour); align code, test and ticket.
findings.check_notes: mapped decision present with rationale; code returns UNVERIFIED iteration_item_may_supply on agent/tool first node, transform stays ERROR; tests match

fix.change: agent/tool first node reading an iteration-filtered field is UNVERIFIED (iteration_item_may_supply); transform stays ERROR; new message template
fix.test: test_contract_simulate.py test_ac9_* (agent, tool, transform, second node; both initial-input values)

decision.outcome: Option 1: a field removed by include_in_iterator_context is UNVERIFIED on an agent or tool first node (the iteration item may supply it); a transform first node stays ERROR; second node onward stays UNVERIFIED; reset removal unchanged
decision.rationale: The whitelist is applied to the parent context but the iteration item is an unknown source for the first node (AC-9, AC-23); a transform does not see the item, and the initial input cannot pass the filter, so the decision is made on node kind, not on unknown_contribution.

findings.title: Write-suppressed blame uses graph-wide suppressions
findings.problem: _absent and _provenance consult self.suppressed, filled by every node the pass visits and keyed by field name only; the suppressing node can be in a sibling branch, downstream, or another component.
findings.impact: A not-guaranteed field is reported as never written to the context, and Provenance.removed_by / mechanism name an unrelated node. Outcome stays ERROR, so only message and provenance are wrong.
findings.recommendation: Consult suppressions only from nodes that are ancestors of the consuming node (record them on the path context), in both _absent and _provenance.
findings.check_notes: suppressions now travel on AbstractContext and merge by path; graph-wide self.suppressed removed; tests added

fix.change: write suppressions travel on AbstractContext and are merged along paths, so only ancestors are blamed

findings.title: Edge walk re-implements leads_to without parity check
findings.problem: Spec decision says edges come from WorkflowNextState.leads_to(); _out_edges re-implements the target walk and never calls it, and no test asserts its target set equals leads_to() on the same fixtures.
findings.impact: A further graph walker can drift from the runtime's definition of reachable targets, silently mis-modelling edges.
findings.recommendation: Add a parity test asserting the _out_edges target set equals WorkflowNextState.leads_to() over the fixtures, or derive the target set from leads_to() and only add kind and path.
findings.check_notes: parity test compares _out_edges targets with leads_to() over eight shapes

fix.change: parity test between _out_edges targets and WorkflowNextState.leads_to()

findings.title: Integer source against number requirement warns
findings.problem: _available_outcome compares declared requirement types with producer types by plain set intersection, so integer against number (or the reverse) has no common element and yields TYPE_MISMATCH although a JSON-schema integer is a valid number.
findings.impact: False WARNING; WARNING blocks in strict mode and counts toward the corpus ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Treat integer as compatible with number in _available_outcome before reporting TYPE_MISMATCH, and add a test for both directions.
findings.check_notes: _types_overlap treats integer as number; both directions tested

fix.change: integer and number are one type in the mismatch comparison; null is ignored there

findings.title: Nullable source never produces a WARNING
findings.problem: AC-7 requires WARNING for a source that is optional or nullable while the consumer requires it. A source whose type list includes null is accepted by the reader, but _available_outcome checks only optional and type mismatch; FieldState carries no nullable flag.
findings.impact: Partial on a required criterion: a nullable source gives OK or UNVERIFIED, and no test covers it.
findings.recommendation: Carry nullability from the reader into FieldState and return the optional/nullable WARNING in _available_outcome when the source type list contains null and the consumer requires a value (AC-7); add a nullable test.
findings.check_notes: _available_outcome warns when a certain source type list has null and the consumer does not accept null; tests added

fix.change: nullable certain source warns (optional_source) unless the consumer accepts null

findings.title: Optional and bare generics in new code
findings.problem: code-quality.md prefers X | None and parameterized generics; new code uses Optional[Callable[[str, Any], None]] (resources.py:33-34, 371, 385) and bare dict/list annotations across contracts/ (effects._bindings, derive._mapping_types, reader._load_document, _schema_fields, _list_contract). The Ruff gate does not select UP rules.
findings.impact: Documented type-hint standard is broken in new code and no automated gate catches it.
findings.recommendation: Annotate as Callable[[str, Any], None] | None and drop Optional from the typing import; parameterize bare dict and list annotations in contracts/ (for example dict[str, object], list[object]).
findings.check_notes: Optional removed from resources.py; bare dict/list annotations parameterized at the cited sites

fix.change: Optional[Callable] to X | None in resources.py; bare dict/list/tuple annotations parameterised in contracts/

findings.impact: Documented cohesion rule for files of about 500 lines or more is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Move _validate_state_input_contracts and INPUT_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR into the contracts package next to input_contract.py and _record_tool_schema into validation/tool_schemas.py, then import them from schema.py and resources.py.
findings.check_notes: input-contract wiring moved to input_contract_stage.py; record_tool_schema moved to tool_schemas.py

fix.change: input-schema stage wiring moved to contracts/input_contract_stage.py; record_tool_schema moved to validation/tool_schemas.py
fix.test: test_input_contract_check.py schema-stage tests; test_tool_schema_resolver.py sink tests

findings.title: AC-40 end-to-end test skipped on a harness it never uses
findings.problem: test_ac40_full_reset_with_an_output_key_saves_with_only_the_key_available carries @requires_harness (skipif on tests/codemie/workflows/test_workflow_templates_validation.py, which is absent), yet its body builds its own WorkflowConfig and calls validate_workflow_with_report. The harness-path corpus run is skipped for the same reason.
findings.impact: A regression in the full save pipeline for a full reset with an output key is caught by no executed test; the ungated corpus run bypasses validate_workflow_with_report.
findings.recommendation: Drop @requires_harness from test_ac40_full_reset_with_an_output_key_saves_with_only_the_key_available and assert report.blocking_records() == [] and the input_schema.result record is OK; gate only tests that call the harness.
findings.check_notes: requires_harness dropped from AC-40 test; runs with _stage_doubles and asserts no blocking records

fix.change: AC-40 end-to-end test ungated and run with the resource stage and executor doubled

findings.title: Timing bounds from the spec are not asserted
findings.problem: Spec requires largest template and a 200-state chain with 20 diamonds within 5x validate_workflow and under 2 s, and 20 built-in lookups warm under 1 s. The chain test uses 100 diamonds and asserts under 10 s; test_tool_schema_resolver.py only records the cold time; the LOOKUP_BUDGET comment still reads provisional.
findings.impact: Performance regressions of the linker on save are not caught by any assertion matching the spec.
findings.recommendation: Assert the spec bounds: largest template and a 200-state chain with 20 diamonds within 5x validate_workflow and under 2 s; assert warm 20 built-in lookups under 1 s in test_tool_schema_resolver.py and refresh the LOOKUP_BUDGET comment.
findings.check_notes: 5x/2 s linker timing tests, 2 s diamond chain test and warm under 1 s lookup assertion added; LOOKUP_BUDGET comment refreshed

fix.change: spec timing bounds asserted: linker within 5x validate_workflow and under 2 s on a 200-state 20-diamond chain and the largest template; warm 20 built-in lookups under 1 s
fix.test: test_contract_corpus.py timing tests; test_contract_simulate.py two-second chain; test_tool_schema_resolver.py warm lookups
